title: There's No Blue Pigment in Blue Eyes #science #body
description:
Every eye colour comes from one brown pigment: melanin. The back layer of the iris is dark in almost everyone; what differs is the front layer (the stroma). Blue eyes have very little melanin there. Its tiny fibres scatter light, blue the most, while the dark back layer absorbs the rest, so blue comes back out: the same physics that makes the sky blue. A little melanin in the front layer gives green or hazel eyes; more gives brown.

Same physics in the sky: Why is the sky blue but sunsets red? https://youtu.be/H_61WImrwoQ

Sources
- American Academy of Ophthalmology (2017), Your Blue Eyes Aren't Really Blue (aao.org)
- Sturm, R. A. & Larsson, M. (2009), Genetics of human iris colour and patterns, Pigment Cell & Melanoma Research 22: 544–562
- Iris colours in the animation are an illustration of the order blue → green → hazel → brown, not measured colours
